```yaml
name: Publish Frontend Types

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  replace-npx-with-pnpx:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v2
        with:
          node-version: '14'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Replace npx with pnpx
        run: find . -type f \( -name "*.sh" -o -name "*.yml" -o -name "*.json" \) -exec sed -i '' 's/npx/pnpx/g' {} +

      - name: Commit changes
        run: |
          git config --global user.name "GitHub Actions"
          git config --global user.email "actions@github.com"
          git add .
          git commit -m "chore: Replace npx with pnpx across the codebase"

      - name: Push changes
        uses: ad-m/github-push-action@v0.6.0
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          branch: main
```

This GitHub Actions workflow will automatically detect when changes are pushed to the `main` branch or when a pull request is opened against the `main` branch. It will then perform the following steps:

1. Check out the repository.
2. Set up Node.js version 14.
3. Install project dependencies using `npm ci`.
4. Recursively search for files with extensions `.sh`, `.yml`, and `.json` and replace all instances of `npx` with `pnpx` using `sed`.
5. Add the modified files to the staging area and commit them with a message indicating the change.
6. Push the committed changes back to the `main` branch.

This ensures that any future commits or merges into the `main` branch will have `pnpx` used instead of `npx`.
